children: A short 11+ English and verbal-reasoning diagnostic for parents and pupils who want a quick snapshot of vocabulary, comprehension, grammar and reasoning skills.
Instructions
Allow 15 minutes.
Work independently.
Do not use a dictionary.
Mark at the end and note which question types caused difficulty.
Questions
1. Closest meaning of “reluctant”: eager, unwilling, noisy, careless.
2. Opposite of “scarce”: rare, plentiful, hidden, valuable.
3. Complete: puppy is to dog as calf is to ____.
4. Which does not belong: violin, trumpet, flute, telescope, piano?
5. Rearrange LISTEN to make another six-letter word.
6. Correct: “Neither of the boys were ready for their test.”
7. Add punctuation: After dinner Mum said we could play outside.
8. “Leo folded the letter twice, pushed it deep into his pocket and changed the subject when his sister entered.” What does this suggest about Leo?
9. If all Fens are Rops and no Rops are Tals, can any Fens be Tals? Explain briefly.
11. Complete: B, E, H, K, __.
12. A book costs £7.50. Three books cost how much?
Answers
1. unwilling
2. plentiful
3. cow or bull: either is an adult animal corresponding to a calf.
4. telescope
5. Examples include SILENT, ENLIST, TINSEL and INLETS. Accept another valid six-letter word using every letter exactly once.
6. “Neither of the boys was ready for their test.” Also accept “his test”. Change “were” to “was”; singular “their” is acceptable.
7. “After dinner, Mum said we could play outside.”
8. He is probably hiding or avoiding something; the hidden letter and changed subject support the inference.
9. No. Every Fen is a Rop, and no Rop can be a Tal.
Score guide

Award one point per question, for a maximum of 12. Accept the alternatives noted in the answers. For question 7, accept other grammatically valid punctuation; an introductory comma is not the only way to punctuate the sentence. For question 8, require a plausible inference supported by a detail from the sentence. These informal bands describe this small sample, not readiness for a particular entrance test.
10–12 a strong starting point on these sampled questions: increase challenge and work on speed and precision.
7–9 some skills demonstrated on these sampled questions: practise the question types that caused mistakes.
4–6 uneven: vocabulary, comprehension or reasoning foundations need targeted work.
0–3 focus on one skill at a time rather than lots of full practice papers.
Different 11+ providers use different formats, so this is a general skills check rather than a prediction for a specific test.
